title: Juice bottle filler, under-fills
tests: Process failure; obvious cause (filler valve and flow meter calibration) is wrong; real cause is air in product at low supply tank level.
summary: Checkweigher rejects rose on a 1 L juice line, with under-fills in clusters. Maintenance replaced two filler valves and recalibrated the flow meter. It did not help. Rejects cluster when the supply tank is below 25%, when the pump draws air; the flow meter reads volume including bubbles.

problem.title: Under-fills on 1 L juice filler, Line 2
problem.whatHappened: Checkweigher rejects for under-fill rose from about 0.2% to 2.6% on Line 2 in the week to 30 May 2026. Rejects came in clusters of 10 to 30 minutes. Two filler valves were replaced and the flow meters were recalibrated with no lasting effect.
problem.where: Filling stage, filler heads and flow meters, and the supply tank to the filler.
problem.when: Clusters mostly in the last hour of each product tank and after a tank change-over.
problem.impact: Under-fill bottles rejected and reworked into the next batch; two batches held for weight checks; schedule loss.
problem.makeModel: Rotary filler, 24 heads with magnetic flow meters
problem.duty: Fills 1 L chilled juice, 6,000 bottles per hour

otherCosts.description: Extra checkweigh and QA hold labour

evidence.title: Checkweigher reject trend, 7 days
evidence.note: Reject bursts at 23:10, 02:40, 05:15 and 13:50; each follows the supply tank falling below about 25%.

evidence.title: Supply tank level trend
evidence.note: Tank at 20 to 25% at each burst. Tank change over at 25%.

evidence.title: Product at the filler bowl
evidence.note: Foam and small bubbles visible in the sight glass during bursts. None at higher level.

evidence.title: Calibration records for flow meters
evidence.note: Recalibrated on 28 May, all within tolerance on the test rig with water.

evidence.title: Work orders for the valves
evidence.note: Heads 7 and 15 valve seals replaced; seals showed normal wear.

children.text: Filler valves worn, not closing or metering properly

actions.description: Replace valves on heads 7 and 15 and recalibrate flow meters

mustSuggest.idea: Air entrained in product when the supply tank is low: pump drawing air or a vortex
Tank change-over at a low level with no minimum level or interlock
Measurement: flow meters measure volume incl. air; no density or deaeration check, and weight check is only at the end
No standard for minimum supply tank level or restart at changeover

acceptable: Supply pump seal or suction leak
Temperature or viscosity change of the product
wrongOrDangerous: Valves worn or meter drift stated as the cause
Operators did not change the tank in time (blame)
Declaring forced deterioration for a method or measurement cause

mustFlag.note: Verified with no evidence; e5 shows normal wear
Flagged with no evidence; e4 shows meters in tolerance
Does not explain bursts tied to tank level

challenge.expectation: Summary points to the evidence the tree has not used: bursts at low tank level and bubbles.
deliberateWeaknesses: n1 verified with no evidence, and e5 shows normal seal wear
n2 flagged root with no evidence; e4 shows meters within tolerance
Obvious cause is wrong: evidence e1 to e3 point to air in the product at low tank level, which no node covers
No materials or method branch: tank level and product change-over practice
Actions are repeat repairs and calibration

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Air in the product from a low supply tank level is a process condition, not wear. The two valve seals showed normal wear.
corrective: Hold and check batches filled during bursts

preventive.what: Minimum supply tank level with tank change-over before the level falls below it
Low-level interlock that pauses the filler or switches tank before air is drawn, and a deaerator or air detection on the filler bowl
In-process fill weight trend with an alarm on bursts, plus a density or air check at the bowl
Tank change-over procedure that checks suction and product level
Check the supply pump suction side for air leaks and seal condition

capa.spares: Not forced. Optional: hold valve seal kits for the filler heads.
capa.rollout: Other filler lines fed from tanks with the same low-level behaviour.
unacceptable: Retrain operators as the only action
